purpose: Make older-adult and family candidate situations distinguishable through concise constraints rather than generic persona text.

paths.title: Pain makes it difficult to keep up the activities I enjoy
paths.description: Activities the person values are difficult to sustain while in pain.

paths.title: I cannot tell whether a home's stated services are actually available for my parent
paths.description: The family needs to distinguish advertised services from support available to their parent.

paths.title: Recovery goals from different professionals do not fit our everyday routine
paths.description: Professional recovery goals conflict with the routine the family can sustain at home.

paths.title: A person helping me threatens to withdraw care if I complain
paths.description: Complaining may put the person’s continued care at risk.

paths.title: My parent's home is difficult for me to help them move around in
paths.description: The home layout makes helping a parent move around difficult.

paths.title: I sleep during the day and struggle to rest at night
paths.description: Daytime sleep and difficulty resting at night disrupt the person’s sleep pattern.

paths.title: Equipment used in rehabilitation is unavailable once my relative returns home
paths.description: Returning home removes access to equipment used during rehabilitation.

paths.title: Chewing makes some of my favourite foods difficult to eat
paths.description: The person wants familiar foods that are now difficult to chew.

paths.title: I cannot explain support needs that occur outside the assessor's visit
paths.description: An assessment visit does not show the support needed at other times.

paths.title: I cannot wash the parts of my body I need to reach
paths.description: The person cannot reach all the areas they need to wash.

paths.title: I cannot arrange trusted local help without being there to meet people
paths.description: The family cannot be present to meet and assess potential local helpers.

paths.title: I cannot tell whether a change in a wound needs urgent attention
paths.description: The person is unsure how urgently a changed wound needs professional attention.

paths.title: The discharge information does not explain who to call about problems at home
paths.description: After discharge, the family lacks a clear contact for problems that arise at home.

paths.title: Family members use different languages and updates do not reach everyone consistently
paths.description: Updates do not reach relatives consistently across the languages they use.

paths.title: Walking far enough to do my errands leaves me exhausted
paths.description: The distance needed for errands exceeds what the person can comfortably manage.

paths.title: I do not know who will help me safely leave an unsafe arrangement
paths.description: The person needs a safe way out but cannot identify who will help.

paths.title: I want someone with me when dying feels frightening
paths.description: Fear of dying creates a wish for someone to remain alongside the person.

paths.title: Pet costs compete with the essentials I need for myself
paths.description: Caring for a pet competes with the person’s own essential spending.

paths.title: My relative is infectious and I do not know how to protect others at home
paths.description: The family lacks a clear way to protect others while caring for an infectious relative.

paths.title: I cannot tell which changes need professional help and which support I can provide
paths.description: The family is uncertain where their support ends and professional help is needed.

paths.title: I do not know what evidence is needed to challenge a care assessment
paths.description: The family cannot identify the evidence required to contest the care assessment.

paths.title: I miss what people say when several people talk at once
paths.description: Overlapping voices make it difficult to follow what others are saying.

paths.title: Meals delivered to me do not match what I enjoy eating
paths.description: Available delivered meals differ from the food the person wants to eat.

paths.title: My relative sees my attempts to help as interference
paths.description: Help offered by the family conflicts with how the relative wants to be involved.

paths.title: I want to stay in my preferred place but cannot arrange the support
paths.description: The support needed to remain in the preferred place cannot be arranged.

paths.title: Pressure discomfort limits how long I can sit or lie in one position
paths.description: Discomfort makes remaining in the same sitting or lying position difficult.

paths.title: Pain wakes me before I have had enough sleep
paths.description: Pain interrupts sleep before the person feels rested.

paths.title: Care schedules conflict with prayer or observances that matter to my relative
paths.description: Care timing clashes with the relative’s valued religious practices.

paths.title: I return home weaker than before and cannot resume my usual routine
paths.description: Reduced strength after returning home makes the previous routine difficult.

paths.title: I cannot find a sleeping position that feels comfortable
paths.description: No available sleeping position feels comfortable to the person.

projection.limits: Projection verifies reachability and preserved metadata. It does not validate occurrence, demand or illustration adequacy.

paths.title: The written decision does not explain how our evidence was considered
paths.description: The family cannot see how its submitted evidence affected the decision.

paths.title: My relative appears more capable during an assessment than on difficult days
paths.description: A relatively capable assessment day differs from days when more support is needed.

paths.title: My relative's needs increase while we wait for a reassessment
paths.description: Support needs grow before the reassessment can take place.

projection.limits: Projection verifies reachability and preserved metadata. It does not validate occurrence, demand or illustration adequacy.

browser_review: Current canonical data loaded in internal browser. Revised movement summaries inspected; all five family care-assessment situations inspected together, with specific constraints. Neutral placeholders remain while generation is paused.
limits: Editorial clarification of existing candidate titles only; no observation, prevalence, quantification, causal or solution claim added.
Hypothesis statuses, research planning, evidence, relationships, media and unrelated records preserved.
Functional projection and browser inspection do not establish venture-builder comprehension or demand.
Remaining generic summaries and neutral illustration placeholders are incomplete work.
No public UI deployment or image generation.
